<ticket source="">
# # Replace the done flag with a three-state status

- Ticket: request
- State: open

## Description

# Replace the done flag with a three-state status

**Type:** refactor with a schema migration

"Done or not" is not enough: people want to see what is in progress. A task gets a status `todo`, `doing` or `done`, which replaces the `done` flag in the data. Clients that still send or read `done` must keep working for one release.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every task in the API has `status`: `"todo"`, `"doing"` or `"done"`, `"todo"` by default.
2. In the database, a `status` column of `tasks` replaces `done`: a new migration adds it, fills it, and drops the `done` column.
3. Existing databases are migrated on startup without losing anything: `done = 1` becomes `done`, `done = 0` becomes `todo`; ids, titles and creation dates are kept.
4. `POST /api/tasks` and `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` accept `status`; any other value answers `400` with `{"error": "status must be todo, doing or done"}`.
5. `GET /api/tasks?status=<value>` lists only the tasks in that status (an unknown value answers the same `400`).
6. Compatibility for one release: responses still include `done` (`true` exactly when the status is `done`); `PATCH` still accepts `done: true` (status `done`) and `done: false` (status `todo`); `GET /api/tasks?done=true|false` keeps working (`false` means not done: `todo` or `doing`).
7. The page shows and changes the status with a select instead of the checkbox, and can filter by status.
8. Tests cover the migration and the API; the README documents `status` and says `done` is deprecated.
</ticket>

plan.summary:
Replace the `done` flag with a three-state `status` (todo, doing, done) in a small Node/SQLite task tracker. The plan has three tasks: back-end, front-end and a final QA pass.

**Back-end (T1)** appends migration #2 to the `migrations` array in `src/db.ts`. It never edits migration 1. The migration adds `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo' CHECK(...)`, fills it (`done=1` becomes `done`, `done=0` becomes `todo`) and drops `done`. It also updates `src/tasks.ts` and `src/app.ts`, and adds the new tests and the README changes. Ids, titles and creation dates are kept, and `user_version` ends at 2. Responses keep a derived `done` boolean, true exactly when the status is `done`, for one more release.

**Decisions I took** where the ticket was silent:
- If `PATCH` has both `status` and `done`, `status` wins.
- If a request has both `?status` and `?done`, `status` wins.
- `POST` takes `status` only; the deprecated `done` is not accepted there.
- An invalid `status` (unknown value, non-string, null or empty) answers 400 `{"error":"status must be todo, doing or done"}` and changes nothing.
- A non-boolean `done` in `PATCH` is ignored, as today.

**A bug the ticket forces us to fix:** `listTasks` currently treats the string "false" as truthy, so `?done=false` returns done tasks. The new code must parse "true" and "false" explicitly.

**Front-end (T2)** touches only `public/index.html` and `public/app.js`. It replaces the checkbox with a select per task (accessible name "Status: <title>") that PATCHes `status`. It also changes the filter to All, To do, Doing, Done, queried through `?status=`.

**QA (T3)** checks every criterion with evidence, including a migration run on a real database file made with the old schema, and adds any missing regression tests.

No blocking questions. Authentication, pagination, extra statuses and removing `done` are out of scope.

acceptance.text: Every task returned by the API has `status` of todo, doing or done; a new task is `todo`.

Migration #2, appended to the migrations array in src/db.ts, adds a `status` column (CHECK of the three values, default 'todo'), fills it from `done` and drops `done`; PRAGMA table_info(tasks) then shows `status` and no `done`.
A database created by migration 1 is migrated on startup: done=1 becomes done, done=0 becomes todo; ids, titles and created_at are kept; user_version becomes 2; reopening changes nothing.
POST /api/tasks and PATCH /api/tasks/:id accept `status`; any other value (unknown string, non-string, null, empty) answers 400 {"error":"status must be todo, doing or done"} and changes nothing.
GET /api/tasks?status=<value> lists only tasks in that status; an unknown value answers the same 400.

For one release: responses include `done` (true iff status is done); PATCH done:true sets status done and done:false sets todo; GET ?done=true returns done tasks and ?done=false returns todo and doing tasks. `status` wins when sent with `done`.
The page uses a select per task (accessible name kept, e.g. "Status: <title>") instead of the checkbox, a change PATCHes `status`, and the filter offers All/To do/Doing/Done and queries ?status=.
Tests cover the migration and the API (AC1-AC6); the README documents `status` and says `done` is deprecated and will be removed next release.

Removing the `done` field and `?done` filter (next release)
New UI design beyond the select and the filter; board or drag-and-drop views

tasks.goal:
Implement the status model end to end on the server, with tests and README.

1. `src/db.ts`: append migration #2 to the `migrations` array (NEVER edit migration 1). It runs inside the existing per-migration transaction. Add the column and drop the old one: `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo' CHECK (status IN ('todo','doing','done'))`; `UPDATE tasks SET status = CASE done WHEN 1 THEN 'done' ELSE 'todo' END`; `ALTER TABLE tasks DROP COLUMN done`. node:sqlite supports ADD/DROP COLUMN. Check that ADD COLUMN with CHECK and NOT NULL DEFAULT works on the Node in use (22.18+); if SQLite refuses, rebuild the table (create tasks_new, copy id, title, status, created_at, drop, rename) while keeping AUTOINCREMENT ids and created_at. user_version must end at 2 and a second open must change nothing.

2. `src/tasks.ts`: export `type Status = 'todo'|'doing'|'done'`, `const STATUSES`, and `isStatus(v: unknown): v is Status`. `Task` becomes `{id, title, status, done, created_at}` where `done = status === 'done'` is derived in `toTask` (Row has `status`, not `done`). `listTasks(db, filter: {status?: Status; done?: boolean})`: `status` wins over `done`; `done:true` => `status='done'`; `done:false` => `status IN ('todo','doing')`. `createTask(db, title, status: Status = 'todo')`. `updateTask(db, id, {title?, status?})`: only `status` reaches this layer; the done-to-status mapping is done in the route.

3. `src/app.ts` contract (the page in T2 relies on it): error body for any bad status is exactly `{"error":"status must be todo, doing or done"}` with HTTP 400, and nothing is changed. GET /api/tasks: if `status` query param is present (even empty) validate it with `isStatus` and answer 400 otherwise; else if `done` is present, parse explicitly `'true'` -> true, `'false'` -> false (do NOT use truthiness: the current code returns done tasks for `?done=false`, which is a bug to fix); any other `done` value is ignored (list all), as today. If both `status` and `done` are sent, `status` wins and `done` is ignored. POST: body.status, when the key is present, must pass `isStatus` (null, empty and non-strings give 400) else defaults to todo; POST does NOT read `done`. PATCH: if `status` key is present validate it first (400 on failure, before any change); if absent and `done === true` use 'done', if `done === false` use 'todo', a non-boolean `done` is ignored; `status` wins when both are present. 404 for a missing task stays as is, and validation order is: parse body, validate status, then look up the task. Every returned task carries `status` and the derived `done` boolean.

4. Tests (node:test, `npm test`): extend `test/tasks.test.ts` for AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6 (default todo; create and patch with each status; 400 for 'bogus', 42, null, '' on POST and PATCH with an unchanged task; ?status filter and its 400; done:true/false on PATCH; status wins over done; ?done=true and ?done=false (todo+doing); `done` derived in responses). Add `test/migration.test.ts` for AC2/AC3: build a `DatabaseSync` file or in-memory db by running the old `CREATE TABLE ... done` DDL by hand with `PRAGMA user_version = 1`, insert rows with done=1 and done=0 and fixed created_at, call `migrate(db)` (exported from src/db.ts), then assert PRAGMA table_info has `status` and no `done`, ids/titles/created_at are unchanged, values are mapped, user_version is 2, and a second `migrate` call is a no-op. Existing tests that assert `done` stay valid through the derived field.

5. `README.md`: update the task shape to include `status` and `done` (with the example), the table rows (`GET ?status=todo|doing|done`, `?done=true|false` deprecated, POST accepts `status`, PATCH accepts `status`), the 400 error body, and a 'Deprecated' note saying `done` (in responses, PATCH body and `?done` filter) is kept for one release and will be removed next release; `status` wins when both are sent. Add the migration to the Layout section's db.ts line if useful. Do not edit public/ (owned by T2).

Replace the checkbox with a status select and make the filter use statuses. Only edit `public/index.html` and `public/app.js` (T1 owns everything else; run in parallel with T1).

Contract with T1 (server): every task from `/api/tasks` is `{id, title, status: 'todo'|'doing'|'done', done: boolean (deprecated, do not use), created_at}`. `GET /api/tasks?status=todo|doing|done` filters; no param lists all. `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` accepts `{status}`. Errors answer `{error: message}` and the existing `api()` helper already throws them; keep `show(err)` for them.

`public/app.js`: in `taskItem` replace the checkbox by a `<select>` with options `todo` 'To do', `doing` 'Doing', `done` 'Done', value set to `task.status`, `aria-label` `Status: ${task.title}` (replaces `Done: ${title}`). On `change` send `PATCH {status: select.value}` then `render`, errors to `show`. In `render`, build the query as `?status=${filter.value}` when the filter has a value (no more `?done=`). A strike-through or muted style on the title for `done` is optional; do not rely on colour alone. Keep the title span, the Delete button, and the layout.

`public/index.html`: the filter select (`#filter`, label 'Show') offers `''` All, `todo` To do, `doing` Doing, `done` Done. Add a small style for the task select if needed (flex layout in li stays). Keep a visible label and keyboard use (native select), no new flow or design beyond this. Verify in a browser by running the app (`npm start` on the worktree $PORT after T1's changes are merged, or against the contract) that changing a status persists after reload and each filter lists the right tasks.

Check every acceptance criterion AC1 to AC8 with evidence, after T1 and T2 are merged. Run `npm test` and report the result. Create a real SQLite file with the OLD schema (migration 1 DDL, user_version 1, rows with done=1 and done=0, known ids, titles and created_at), start the app on it (`DB_PATH=<file> PORT=$PORT npm start`, in the background, stopped afterwards), and confirm: the rows are migrated, ids, titles and created_at are kept, `PRAGMA table_info(tasks)` shows `status` and no `done`, user_version is 2, and a restart changes nothing. With curl (skill termf:curl) check: default todo; POST/PATCH with each status; 400 body exactly `{"error":"status must be todo, doing or done"}` for bogus, numeric, null and empty values, task unchanged afterwards; `?status=` filter and its 400; `done` in responses; PATCH done:true/false; `?done=true` and `?done=false` (the latter returns todo and doing); status wins over done on PATCH and on GET. Check the page: the select per task has the accessible name `Status: <title>`, changing it persists, and the filter lists All/To do/Doing/Done and filters correctly; keyboard-only operation works. Check the README documents `status` and the `done` deprecation. Add missing regression tests in `test/` only where a criterion is not yet covered (do not rewrite T1's tests) and do not change source files: report any defect to the lead with the repro.

reviews.summary:
I found nothing that must change. I read the full diff of src/, public/, README and both test files. I checked each criterion (AC1 to AC8) against the code rather than trusting the earlier reports.

- **Migration:** migration #2 is appended and migration 1 is untouched. It runs inside the existing transaction with the `user_version` bump, so it rolls back as a whole on failure. The column has the CHECK and the 'todo' default, the fill maps done=1 to done and everything else to todo, and `done` is dropped. Ids, titles and creation dates are never touched.
- **API:**
  - Every bad `status` (unknown, non-string, null, empty) gets the exact 400 body on POST, PATCH and `GET ?status=`.
  - PATCH validates `status` before it touches the task, so a bad value changes nothing.
  - `status` wins over `done` on PATCH and on GET.
  - `?done=false` now returns todo and doing tasks. The old string-truthiness bug is fixed because the value is parsed explicitly.
  - Responses carry `done`, true exactly when the status is done.
- **Page:** each task has a native select named "Status: <title>" that PATCHes `status`. The filter offers All, To do, Doing and Done and queries `?status=`. The page no longer sends or reads `done`.
- **README and tests:** the README documents `status` and the `done` deprecation. The tests go through the real HTTP API and a hand-built old-schema database, and they map to AC1 to AC6.
- **Reports:** T3's evidence (a real old-schema file, a restart that changes nothing, the curl checks and a browser run) fits the code. I did not re-run it.

I did not run `npm test`, a typecheck (TypeScript is not installed) or the page in a browser. I did not run an accessibility scan. T3 did not press arrow keys on the select, and I did not either.

One thing I noticed but did not report: a PATCH or POST body of JSON `null` makes `"status" in body` throw. The old `body.title` did the same, so it is not new.

report.summary:
Scope: replace `tasks.done` with a three-state `status` (todo/doing/done) across the DB (src/db.ts), queries (src/tasks.ts), routes (src/app.ts), page (public/index.html, public/app.js), tests and README. I changed nothing.

Acceptance criteria (each checkable; source = ticket AC of the same number):
- AC1: every task returned by the API has `status` in todo|doing|done; a new task is `todo`.
- AC2: migration #2 appended to the `migrations` array (never edit migration 1) adds `status`, fills it from `done`, drops `done`. After it, `PRAGMA table_info(tasks)` has `status` and no `done`. Status column should carry a CHECK of the three values and DEFAULT 'todo'.
- AC3: starting on a database made by migration 1 (with done=1 and done=0 rows) keeps ids, titles, created_at; done=1→done, 0→todo; user_version becomes 2; running again changes nothing.
- AC4: POST and PATCH accept `status`; any other value (including a non-string, null or empty) answers 400 `{"error":"status must be todo, doing or done"}` and changes nothing.
- AC5: `GET /api/tasks?status=X` returns only that status; unknown value gives the same 400.
- AC6: responses also carry `done` (true iff status is done); PATCH `done:true`→done, `done:false`→todo; `?done=true` → done only; `?done=false` → todo and doing.
- AC7: page uses a select per task instead of the checkbox (accessible name kept, e.g. "Status: <title>"), a change PATCHes `status`, and the filter offers All/To do/Doing/Done and queries `?status=`.
- AC8: tests cover migration (AC2/3) and API (AC1,4,5,6); README documents `status` and marks `done` deprecated (removal next release).

Decisions taken (my reasons):
- PATCH with both `status` and `done`: `status` wins (per triage). Validation of `status` happens first.
- `?status` together with `?done`: `status` wins, `done` ignored.
- POST also accepts the deprecated `done` is NOT required by the ticket: POST takes `status` only (default todo).
- Invalid `done` in PATCH (non-boolean) is ignored as today.

Bug that AC6 forces fixing: today `listTasks` does `filter.done ? 1 : 0` on the string "false", which is truthy, so `?done=false` currently returns done tasks. The new code must parse "true"/"false" explicitly.

Out of scope: auth, pagination, other statuses, removing `done` (next release), new UI design beyond select/filter, drag/board view.

report.summary:
The server now has a three-state `status` (todo, doing, done) in place of the `done` flag, with the README and tests updated. `npm test` passes: 25 tests, 0 failures, 18 of them new. I could not run a typecheck, because `typescript` is not installed here (`npx tsc` refuses to run). I did not edit `public/`.

- **Migration (`src/db.ts`):** I appended migration #2 and left migration 1 alone. It adds `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo' CHECK(status IN (...))`, fills it from `done` (1 becomes `done`, 0 becomes `todo`) and drops `done`. ADD and DROP COLUMN work as-is on Node 22.20, so no table rebuild was needed. `user_version` ends at 2, and ids, titles and `created_at` are kept.
- **Queries (`src/tasks.ts`):** it exports `Status`, `STATUSES` and `isStatus`. `Task` is `{id, title, status, done, created_at}`, with `done` derived as `status === 'done'`. `listTasks` takes `{status?, done?}`, `status` wins, and `done:false` means todo or doing. `createTask` takes a status. `updateTask` takes `{title?, status?}`.
- **Routes (`src/app.ts`):**
  - **Bad status:** any bad status answers 400 `{"error":"status must be todo, doing or done"}` and changes nothing. That covers `GET ?status=` (including an empty value), POST, and PATCH. PATCH validates the status before the task lookup, so an unknown task id with a bad status gives 400, not 404.
  - **Deprecated `done`:** `?done` is parsed explicitly, so `?done=false` now returns todo and doing tasks. It used to return done tasks, which was a bug. Any other `?done` value is ignored. PATCH maps `done:true` to `done` and `done:false` to `todo`, ignores a non-boolean `done`, and lets `status` win when both are sent. POST ignores `done`.
- **Tests:** `test/tasks.test.ts` covers AC1, AC4, AC5 and AC6 through the HTTP API. The new `test/migration.test.ts` builds the old schema by hand and checks the column swap, the value mapping, kept ids and dates, `user_version` 2, a no-op second run, the CHECK constraint and a fresh database.
- **README:** it documents `status`, the new table rows, the 400 body and a Deprecated section saying `done` is removed next release.

The page in `public/` still sends `done` and reads `done`. That keeps working through the compatibility layer until T2 changes it.

public/app.js still sends and reads `done`; it keeps working via the compatibility layer until T2 switches it to `status`.

I found nothing that must change. I read the full diff of src/, public/, README and both test files. I checked each criterion (AC1 to AC8) against the code rather than trusting the earlier reports.

- **Migration:** migration #2 is appended and migration 1 is untouched. It runs inside the existing transaction with the `user_version` bump, so it rolls back as a whole on failure. The column has the CHECK and the 'todo' default, the fill maps done=1 to done and everything else to todo, and `done` is dropped. Ids, titles and creation dates are never touched.
- **API:**
  - Every bad `status` (unknown, non-string, null, empty) gets the exact 400 body on POST, PATCH and `GET ?status=`.
  - PATCH validates `status` before it touches the task, so a bad value changes nothing.
  - `status` wins over `done` on PATCH and on GET.
  - `?done=false` now returns todo and doing tasks. The old string-truthiness bug is fixed because the value is parsed explicitly.
  - Responses carry `done`, true exactly when the status is done.
- **Page:** each task has a native select named "Status: <title>" that PATCHes `status`. The filter offers All, To do, Doing and Done and queries `?status=`. The page no longer sends or reads `done`.
- **README and tests:** the README documents `status` and the `done` deprecation. The tests go through the real HTTP API and a hand-built old-schema database, and they map to AC1 to AC6.

I did not run `npm test`, a typecheck (TypeScript is not installed) or the page in a browser. I did not run an accessibility scan. T3 did not press arrow keys on the select, and I did not either.

report.summary:
No confirmed vulnerabilities. I read the diff of src/ and public/ against c2324d0. I did not run tests or an npm audit, and I did not review the tests or README.

What I checked:
- SQL injection (A05:2025): every query is parameterised. The status filter strings are fixed literals, and `status` is allowlisted by `isStatus` before it reaches SQL. The migration is static SQL.
- Input validation (A10:2025): a bad `status` on POST, PATCH or GET returns 400 before any write. The CHECK constraint on the column is a second control. A non-boolean `done` is ignored and `?done` is parsed strictly. This fails closed.
- XSS (A05:2025): public/app.js sets titles through `textContent` and option text through `textContent`. The status comes from the server's allowlisted values. The filter value goes into the URL through `encodeURIComponent`. There is no innerHTML.
- Dependencies (A03:2025): none added.
- Access control (A01:2025): the app has no authentication, which the ticket puts out of scope. No new endpoint or object lookup was added.
- Migration integrity: it runs in the existing transaction, so a failure rolls back.

Candidate not confirmed, low: a request body of JSON `null` makes `"status" in body` throw on POST and PATCH. The old `body.title` did the same. What settles it is whether `readJson` or the server's top-level error handler turns the throw into a 500 and keeps the process alive. I did not trace that. The worst case is a 500 or a request that fails to answer, with no data exposure. It existed before the change.

Not covered: no runtime exploitation, no review of the tests or README, no check of request body size limits, which `readJson` was not changed to touch.
